extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers interested in comedy, literary critics, and students of humour
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and distinctions for recognising, producing, and judging the Comic (as distinct from satire, irony, and humour) in literature and stage work; includes tests of comic perception, aims of the comic poet, and stylistic guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to perceive ridicule in those you love without loving them less
rubrics_metrics.description: You may estimate your capacity for Comic perception by being able to detect the ridicule of them you love, without loving them less: and more by being able to see yourself somewhat ridiculous in dear eyes, and accepting the correction their image of you proposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test of comic sensibility: recognise the ridiculous in intimates and in yourself and accept it kindly. Example: affectionate couples perceiving the comic in quarrel and joining hands promptly. Anti-pattern: if detection chills kindliness, you slip into satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish Comic from Satire, Irony, and Humour
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comic is a perceptive governing spirit distinct from satire, irony, and humour; it enfolds thinner forms of them but differs in method and aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire 'falls foul' and lashes to make the subject writhe; Irony 'stings under a semi-caress' making the subject doubt whether he is hurt; Humour embraces and pities while exposing. Do not confuse these modes when evaluating or composing comic work; choose the mode by desired moral/directive effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satire as moral and combative (anti-pattern to Comic)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Satirist is a moral agent, often a social scavenger, working on a storage of bile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire aims to wound or correct by attack; if the response to a comic perception is to chill kindness and strike heavy blows, the work is satiric rather than comic. Example: a man of deep wit condemned by opposite party becomes satiric rather than comic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irony should be ambiguous and tasteful, not foppish or leering
rubrics_metrics.description: Irony is the humour of satire; it may be savage with a moral object (Swift) or sedate with a malicious (Gibbon). The foppish irony fretting to be seen, and the irony which leers, are failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use irony to hint or sting beneath apparent civility; avoid overtly showy or leering irony which betrays intention and fails to achieve subtlety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humour as compassionate exposure and fusion with tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: If you laugh all round him, tumble him, roll him about, deal him a smack, and drop a tear on him... it is a spirit of Humour that is moving you. The humourist of high order fuses the Tragic sentiment with the Comic narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humour combines pity with exposure and can include the tragic; great humourists (e.g., Don Quixote) elicit both heart and mind. Aim for humane warmth alongside ridicule rather than cold attack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic addresses the intellect and quickens it by contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comic is addressed to the intellect: there is no humour in Alceste and Tartuffe; they refresh the intellect by force of the contrast they offer between themselves and the wiser world about them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy should present clear intellectual contrasts between character and society; value comes from interpretation and perception rather than mere physical comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: Comic poet works in a narrow social field and present moment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comic poet is in the narrow field, or enclosed square, of the society he depicts; he is not concerned with beginnings or endings or surroundings, but with what you are now weaving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedies should concentrate on social character and present situations; avoid sprawling epic scope or irrelevant backstory that diffuses the comic perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim: awaken thoughtful laughter (test of true Comedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: One excellent test of the civilization of a country... I take to be the flourishing of the Comic idea and Comedy; and the test of true Comedy is that it shall awaken thoughtful laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True comedy provokes reflective amusement (a smile or thought-through laugh) rather than mere noisy hilarity. When judging works, prefer those that prompt reflection alongside amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: impersonal, polite laughter nearer a smile
rubrics_metrics.description: The laughter of Comedy is impersonal and of unrivalled politeness, nearer a smile; often no more than a smile. It laughs through the mind, for the mind directs it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comic tone should be civil and measured; prefer subtle smiling irony over coarse derision. Anti-patterns: scornful, brutal laughter or loud stormy fun that lacks intellectual light.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid derisive laughter at misfortune or the fundamentally unfortunate
rubrics_metrics.description: Incidents casting ridicule on our unfortunate nature instead of our conventional life provoke derisive laughter, which thwarts the Comic idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make victims of the unfortunate the butt of comedy; comic perception targets affectations, pretensions, and misapplied pretence, not mere poverty or misfortune.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require a sober liking of humanity and tempered moral aim
rubrics_metrics.description: To understand his work and value it, you must have a sober liking of your kind and a sober estimate of our civilized qualities... The aim and business of the Comic poet are misunderstood when he is accused of dishonouring our nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedic creators should approach subjects with humane sympathy and restraint rather than spite. The comic should correct by illumination, not degrade by malice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and taste (mesure et gout) are essential
rubrics_metrics.description: The French lay marked stress on mesure et gout, and they own how much they owe to Moliere for leading them in simple justness and taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedic writing needs proportion and refined taste; avoid excess, grossness, or overblown sentiment that misapplies comic force. Use Molière as a model for measured comic restraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic perception manifests as a 'Spirit overhead' observing social disproportion
rubrics_metrics.description: When contemplating men, discern a Spirit overhead... whenever they wax out of proportion, overblown, affected, pretentious... the Spirit overhead will look humanely malign and cast an oblique light on them, followed by volleys of silvery laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate comedy by whether it perceives and subtly illuminates disproportion or pretension in social behaviour rather than merely exploiting it for vulgar laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic writing for the stage enforces clarity, plan, and English
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing for the stage would be a corrective of a too-incrusted scholarly style... It keeps minor writers to a definite plan, and to English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stage discipline (clear scheme, economy, present action) as a corrective when producing comic prose; stage-craft promotes intelligibility and comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic effect often arises from intellectual pleading of doubtful causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of doubtful causes in contest are open to Comic interpretation, and any intellectual pleading of a doubtful cause contains germs of an Idea of Comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argumentative or plausibly defended absurdities can be mined for comedy by exposing the contrast between formality of defense and the underlying folly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience refinement measured by what and how they laugh
rubrics_metrics.description: We know the degree of refinement in men by the matter they will laugh at, and the ring of the laugh; the larger natures are distinguished by the great breadth of their power of laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating and cultivating comedy, attend to audience taste and cultivate laughter that indicates breadth and refinement rather than narrow, coarse mirth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid confusing realism-for-realism's-sake with comic interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern French comedy is commendable for the directness of the study of actual life... A consequence of this crude, though well-meant, realism is the collision of the writers in their scenes and incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Realism must be guided by comic idea and measured taste; mere faithful depiction ('the fly in amber') is less portable or illuminating than a comedy shaped by the comic perception.
